name: baseline-fla-chunk
desc: FLA chunk_kda Triton prefill baseline (Kimi K3 KDA layer: H=96 K=V=128)
evidence: kda-serving/baseline_matrix.csv: 3.0-3.3M tok/s flat over T=1K-64K, B=1-8; chunked prefill 1.005x monolithic

name: baseline-fla-recurrent
desc: FLA fused_recurrent_kda decode baseline (state-carry, T=1 steps)
evidence: kda-serving/baseline_matrix.csv: 0.05ms/step flat vs ctx (1K/8K/32K); B=1-8 launch-bound 50us; B>=32 state-BW-bound, throughput plateaus ~208K tok/s

name: OPT-TARGET: decode large-B state bandwidth
desc: B>=32 per-step latency scales ~linearly with B — state read+write dominates. Candidates: persistent-state kernel (skip state spill), fp8 state, fuse beta/gate into decode kernel, batch heads into fewer launches

name: OPT-TARGET: decode small-B launch overhead
desc: 50us/step floor at B<=8 is launch-bound (state only 3MB). Candidates: CUDA-graph capture, multi-step fused recurrent, head-dim tiling improvements

name: OPT-TARGET: prefill kernel efficiency
desc: ~3.3M tok/s ceiling = ~103 TFLOP/s effective on delta-rule MACs — well under MI355X bf16 peak; targets: WY-representation GEMM tiling for gfx950 mfma, fused gate-exp epilogue

name: NEXT: aiter-JIT KDA kernel
reason: aiter 0.1.9 JIT build broken on this box (aiter<->composable_kernel mismatch, see kernel-lab/kda-attn findings)

name: flydsl-decode-v1
desc: FlyDSL (MLIR) decode-step kernel: one workgroup per (B,H), 128 threads own state rows, fused L2N + decay + delta-rule + o reduction; scalar v1
evidence: correct: 3-step fp64 carry state rRMSE 3e-07, o rRMSE 0.0016 (better than fla 0.004); perf: 0.10-0.31x vs fla on ctx=32K grid (scalar memory access)
next: v2: vec4 loads/stores, single S read per chunk (dec in registers), CHUNK=32, fold o into pass 1

name: flydsl-decode-v2
desc: vec4 single-read state, registers carry dec, CHUNK=32, o-reduction folded into pass 1
evidence: correct (state rRMSE 3e-07, identical to v1); 0.22-0.50x vs fla (v1 was 0.10-0.31x); B=128 0.50x
next: v3: coalesced state stores (transpose via smem: stage 4 rows per write group, or 64-thread quad owns 4 rows with contiguous vec4 store); shrink critical path via warp shuffle reductions (fx.numeric shuffle_xor) to cut barriers

name: flydsl-decode-v3
desc: fused-o algebra (od reduction merged into kv pass) + global-address-ordered coalesced stores
reason: 0.30-0.31x vs fla = ~1.6x SLOWER than v2 (0.50x). Added smem traffic (od dual-staging) and store staging round-trip outweigh gains. Revert to v2 as FlyDSL best.
lesson: strided scalar stores were NOT the real bottleneck (write-back L2 absorbs them); the real v2 gap vs fla is elsewhere (likely fla's block-level Triton ops compiling to better LDS/wave scheduling)

name: flydsl-track-status
desc: FlyDSL toolchain proven: 3 correct kernels built and evidence-iterated; best = v2 at 0.22-0.50x of fla
evidence: v1 0.10-0.31x -> v2 0.22-0.50x -> v3 rejected. Remaining gap vs fla likely requires fla-style block-level staging or HIP C++ (next escalation tier)

name: flydsl-decode-v6
desc: 256-thread column-split: wavefront w owns 8-col group, lane owns rows 2l/2l+1; trees complete within wavefront -> 0 barriers, 0 smem, ~200 ops/lane
evidence: kernel 9.1/33.2/496us vs FLA 6.1/19.3/311 = 1.49/1.72/1.60x (gap was 2.6-3.3x in v4); correct first-compile (state rRMSE 7.8e-08)
next: v7a: hybrid lane layout (16 rows x 4 cols per lane, tree depth 3, ~56 vs 192 tree-ops) + CUDA-graph bench mode; v7b: bf16-state variant for large-B (path B, user-approved)

name: v7a-hybrid-layout-design
desc: lane=16rows x 4cols, depth-3 trees over 8-lane groups
reason: paper analysis: 64 state regs/lane -> 16+16 vec4 FMA partials + 16 update = ~345 lane-ops vs v6's ~200 (partial-FMA growth 4x beats tree savings 96->21). Rejected before writing code. Tree-latency gain (3 vs 6 steps) not worth register/occupancy cost.

name: flydsl-decode-v7
evidence: graphed wall: B=1 1.06x (first cell win), B=2 0.86x, B=4-128 0.58-0.71x; kernel 1.45-1.70x unchanged; graphed-FLA at 5.1TB/s = HBM limit
next: v8: bf16 state variant (Path B) + BW tuning for B>=32; accuracy report mandatory
